title: Distinguish human-authorized decisions from agent-recorded advisory
context: Agents were able to create or re-record decisions without human consent, potentially stripping human signatures or creating binding policy unilaterally. The system needs trustworthy authority boundaries.
decision: Introduce two record types by authorship: human_confirmed (requires consumed capture token, carries veto authority) vs agent_recorded (advisory only, never authoritative). Authority is sticky—once a human vouches for a decision, agents cannot downgrade it by re-recording.
consequences: Agents can create advisory decisions but cannot produce binding policy unilaterally
Human decisions survive re-record with authority intact—agents cannot strip human signatures
Clear authority hierarchy prevents unintended agent overrides of human choices
Decision provenance and trust level persist across all system mutations
alternatives_rejected: Single decision type regardless of source—enables agents to accidentally or maliciously acquire human authority
Authorship metadata without authority differentiation—doesn't prevent misuse at enforcement layer
Allow re-record to downgrade authority—creates silent failures and loses human intent
